summary:
North Sulawesi stands under Indonesia's national framework, and the national laws described in the Indonesia record apply to visitors to this province. The sources reviewed contain no North Sulawesi-specific provincial regulation on gender identity or sexual orientation.

OutRight Action International's mapping of Indonesia's national laws and discriminatory regional regulations (Katjasungkana and Wieringa, 2022) examined regional regulations in eight focus provinces: Aceh, DKI Jakarta, East Kalimantan, Lampung, North Sumatra, South Sulawesi, South Sumatra and Yogyakarta. North Sulawesi was not among them. The study documented significant regional variation in dress codes, curfews and restrictions on where transgender people may appear, and states that its findings are valid for regions beyond the focus set, but no such provincial restriction is documented for North Sulawesi itself.

Police conduct in Manado is documented through a local account. On 11 June 2016 LGBT groups joined the city's women's movement in a street action against sexual violence at Bundaran Zero Point, running from 08.00 to 10.00 WITA, with SALUT (Sanubari Sulawesi Utara), the local LGBT organisation, taking part. The same reporting records that police raids in Manado have included harassment of LGBT people: SALUT's director Coco Jericho reported that a butch lesbian was groped during a raid. Victims often do not report such conduct because they fear their families will not accept their orientation. No arrests or prosecutions are reported in that account.

Public visibility by trans people in the province is documented at official level. On Saturday 10 November 2012 a waria beach-queen pageant was held at Malalayang beach in Manado, organised by Indonesian parliament member Paula Sinjal together with the National Narcotics Agency of North Sulawesi as an outreach event on the dangers of drugs and HIV/AIDS. Sinjal was quoted saying that waria are among local people and deserve attention. No adverse official action is recorded in connection with the event.

Media stigma following public visibility is documented in a 2024 Konde.co interview with Alexa, elected Ratu Waria Sulawesi Utara for 2016 to 2018 at the Sahid Kawanua Hotel in Manado. She states that after her title she suffered discrimination from sensationalist media and from the public, with her personal crisis peaking around 25 March 2019. No legal or police action appears anywhere in her account. The most recent incident documented in these sources dates from 2019 and was published in February 2024; no later instance is documented.
tangentialFactors:
OutRight Action International's 2022 mapping found substantial regional variation across Indonesia in how regional regulations restrict transgender people, with dress codes, curfews and limits on where transgender people may appear appearing in some provinces and not others. North Sulawesi falls outside the eight focus provinces examined, so the province's position relative to those documented restrictions is not established by that study.

The Manado raid-harassment account is a single local report from 2016 and describes conduct reported by one organisation; it records no arrests, charges or prosecutions. The 2012 pageant and the 2016 street action show organised, visible LGBT and waria participation in Manado civic life in the same period.
localsOnly:
SALUT (Sanubari Sulawesi Utara) operates as the local LGBT organisation in North Sulawesi and has publicly documented raid-related harassment, including the groping of a butch lesbian during a police raid, as well as the reluctance of victims to report because of family rejection.

Trans women in the province have an established public presence: a waria beach-queen pageant was held at Malalayang beach in Manado on 10 November 2012, organised by a member of the national parliament with the National Narcotics Agency of North Sulawesi, and a Ratu Waria Sulawesi Utara is elected at a Manado hotel, the title held by Alexa for 2016 to 2018.

Residents who are publicly visible as waria report discrimination from sensationalist media and from the public after receiving such titles, with Alexa describing her personal crisis peaking around 25 March 2019. LGBT groups in Manado have also joined the city's women's movement in public street actions, including the anti-sexual-violence action at Bundaran Zero Point on 11 June 2016.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether North Sulawesi has issued any provincial regulation restricting dress, curfew or the appearance of transgender people is unresolved: the OutRight Action International study did not include the province in its eight focus provinces, and no other source in this inventory addresses provincial regulation here.

Whether police raids in Manado continue after 2016, and whether any arrests or prosecutions of LGBT or waria people have occurred in North Sulawesi, are not sourced. The 2016 report records harassment during raids but no charges, and no later enforcement action appears in the inventory.

No incident, survey figure or official statement from North Sulawesi later than the events described in the February 2024 Konde.co interview is documented here; the province's current enforcement climate is not established by these sources.
